description: A general counsel must approve the company's response plan to a civil subpoena seeking customer analytics records, including counsel selection, privilege handling, data redaction, and protection of sensitive source code.

shared_context.S1: The company received a civil subpoena seeking customer analytics records, related communications, and a source-code appendix.
shared_context.S2: The subpoena requires a written response within 10 calendar days.
shared_context.S3: Elena Brooks approves the company's response strategy and any commitments made to the requesting party.
shared_context.S4: At the case team's routine pre-response review, Elena asks investigations, e-discovery, and the business litigation liaison to report any issue that must be addressed before the response is approved.

PF1.text: Nikhil completed a conflict-database check this morning and confirmed that the company's usual outside litigation firm, Harrison & Cole, currently represents the subpoenaing party in an unrelated matter; the firm's conflict prevents it from advising on this subpoena, and Merritt Legal has been cleared as the replacement, but Nikhil has not yet circulated the check result.

PF2.text: Marisol's document review found exactly 47 attorney-client privileged emails in the responsive collection and exactly 312 customer records containing Social Security numbers; she has not added those counts to the draft response spreadsheet because quality control of the export finished after the spreadsheet was sent to the case team.

PF3.text: During yesterday's meeting, the product vice president instructed Tara that the source-code appendix must not be produced until a protective order restricting access to outside counsel and experts is entered; the appendix contains the unreleased scoring logic that the product team considers its most sensitive trade secret, and Tara has not put that instruction in the response draft.

acceptance_conditions: Merritt Legal must be appointed to advise on the subpoena response.
The response plan must encode exactly 47 privileged emails as withheld.
The response plan must encode exactly 312 customer records as redacted for Social Security numbers.
A protective order must be required before producing the source-code appendix.
The source-code appendix must not be produced before the protective order is entered.
The response plan's privileged-email withholding count must be 47.
The response plan's customer-record redaction count must be 312.
The response plan must encode the protective-order requirement and prohibit source-code production before entry of that order.

decisive_facts.why: The ordinary choice would be to keep Harrison & Cole on the matter; PF1 changes the appointed firm to exactly Merritt Legal because Harrison & Cole has a disqualifying conflict.
The response changes from unspecified privilege handling and data review to encoding exactly 47 privileged emails as withheld and exactly 312 customer records as redacted.
The source-code response changes from possible production with the subpoena materials to requiring a protective order first and setting source-code production before that order to false.
